summary: Verified logbook_filter() backward-compatibility fix for QSOs missing 'logbook' field. Both backend (8/8 pytest) and frontend flows pass. Admin's 10 seeded QSOs (with logbook field removed to simulate production) appear correctly under Radioamateur and are excluded from CB/SWL.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 1356 lines — consider splitting into routers (auth, qso, admin, adif) for maintainability.
logbook_filter() only handles missing-field fallback for 'radioamateur'; if a future default changes, this coupling should be documented via a constant DEFAULT_LOGBOOK.
Login response returns access_token in body but no auth cookie is set — mixed strategy vs. Auth-testing playbook that expects httpOnly cookies. Verify intended design.
seed_data_creation: None; used existing seeded admin QSOs (10 QSOs, 7 unique callsigns) with logbook field previously $unset by main agent to simulate production data.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Auth uses Bearer token from POST /api/auth/login (access_token in JSON body). No auth cookie is set. Frontend logbook selector is a native <select> — use page.locator('select').select_option('radioamateur'|'cb'|'swl'). Stats endpoint returns {total_qsos, total_callsigns}. All 8 backend tests in test_logbook_filter.py pass; the file is safe to reuse as a regression suite.
rca of the issue: Before fix: MongoDB query {logbook: 'radioamateur'} did not match legacy QSOs lacking the field, so F4MVD (and all pre-multi-logbook users) saw 0 QSOs while admin panel still counted them. Fix in server.py:99 logbook_filter() returns {'$or': [{logbook:'radioamateur'},{logbook:{$exists:false}}]} so legacy documents are treated as radioamateur. CB/SWL keep strict {logbook: X} match so they remain empty. Verified via 8 pytest cases and end-to-end UI switching Ham→CB→Ham→SWL.
